answer: One defense is continuous behavioral delta scoring against a public atlas: the network publishes baselines of how honest agents behave - tool mix, timing, counterparties - and each agent emits a live signal of its activity that is scored against its own baseline. If two identities' signals track each other too closely, their delta collapses and both lose weight, since genuine agents drift apart while clones march in lockstep. An attacker must therefore make every fake behave distinctly, in real time, which means staffing each with real, varied work instead of copying one script.
